# Church Finance Policy — Draft

**Church:** [Church name]  
**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Approved by:** [Board/elders/authorized governing body]  
**Review date:** [Date, at least annually]

> This is a working template, not legal or accounting advice. Fill in the bracketed items and have the appropriate governing body and a qualified local accountant or attorney review it before adoption. Requirements for churches, charitable organizations, payroll, and donations vary by location.

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how the church budgets, receives, spends, safeguards, and reports funds. It applies to staff, officers, ministry leaders, volunteers, and anyone handling church money or financial records.

Church funds must be used for the church’s approved purposes and handled transparently, with appropriate records and separation of duties.

## 2. Financial oversight

The [Board/Finance Committee/authorized governing body] is responsible for financial oversight. Its responsibilities include:

- Approving the annual budget and material changes to it.
- Reviewing financial reports at least [monthly/quarterly].
- Monitoring cash balances, obligations, and budget variances.
- Ensuring financial controls are followed and arranging an independent review at least [annually].
- Approving bank accounts, authorized signers, credit arrangements, and financial-system access.

The [Treasurer/Finance Lead] maintains or oversees the books, prepares reports, and ensures transactions are documented. The person who records a transaction should not be its sole approver or sole reviewer of the related bank reconciliation.

## 3. Budget and spending authority

The governing body approves an annual budget before the start of each fiscal year. Spending should follow that budget and the approval limits below.

| Transaction | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Up to $[amount] | Budget owner or ministry leader |
| $[amount]–$[amount] | [Finance Lead/Treasurer] |
| Over $[amount] | [Two authorized approvers/Board] |
| Unbudgeted expense over $[amount] | [Board/authorized body] |
| Any related-party transaction | Disinterested approvers, as described in Section 8 |

No one may approve their own reimbursement, payment, or purchase. Approvals must be recorded in writing or in the church’s financial system. Transactions may not be split to avoid an approval limit.

## 4. Payments and purchases

Payments should be made by check, electronic transfer, or an approved church payment method. Cash payments should be avoided except for small, documented exceptions approved by [role].

Every payment must have supporting documentation, such as an invoice, receipt, contract, or approved reimbursement request. The documentation should state the business purpose, budget category, amount, and approver.

Contracts, leases, loans, recurring commitments, and purchases over $[amount] require approval from [role/body] before the church commits to them. Only authorized signers may bind the church.

## 5. Reimbursements

A person seeking reimbursement must submit an itemized request with original or electronic receipts and a description of the church purpose within [number] days of the expense. The request must be approved by someone other than the person seeking reimbursement.

Reimbursements are limited to reasonable, necessary expenses incurred for approved church activity. Personal expenses, undocumented expenses, and expenses outside the approved purpose will not be reimbursed unless an authorized exception is documented.

Mileage and other travel reimbursements will follow the church’s approved rates and applicable local requirements: [state rate or reference].

## 6. Bank accounts, cards, and online access

Church funds must be held in accounts titled in the church’s legal name, where applicable. Personal accounts must not be used to hold church funds.

The governing body approves account signers and reviews the list at least annually and whenever a signer leaves their role. Bank statements and reconciliations must be reviewed monthly by someone who does not handle all of the related transactions.

Church cards and online payment access may be issued only with approval from [role/body]. They are for authorized church expenses only. Cardholders must submit itemized receipts promptly and may not share credentials or cards. Lost cards or suspected unauthorized transactions must be reported immediately to [role] and the financial institution.

## 7. Donations and other receipts

Donations and other receipts must be recorded promptly, deposited intact, and deposited into a church account. Cash and checks should be counted by two unrelated people when practical. The count and deposit should be documented, and the people counting should not be the only people recording or reconciling the deposit.

Donor-restricted funds must be tracked separately in the records and used only for the stated restriction, subject to applicable law and the church’s accepted gift practices. Donation acknowledgments and records will be handled in accordance with applicable requirements and the church’s privacy practices.

The church does not promise that a gift is tax-deductible unless that status is confirmed under applicable law.

## 8. Conflicts of interest and related-party transactions

Anyone with a personal or financial interest in a proposed transaction must disclose it before discussion or approval. The interested person must not approve the transaction and should not participate in the decision, except to provide requested factual information.

The disinterested approvers must determine that the transaction is in the church’s interest, reasonable, and appropriately documented. Disclosures and decisions must be recorded in meeting minutes or the financial record.

## 9. Payroll and worker payments

Payroll, contractor payments, expense allowances, and required filings must be administered by authorized personnel using accurate records and in accordance with applicable law. Worker classification and compensation arrangements should be reviewed by qualified local advisers when needed.

Changes to compensation or payroll details require approval by [role/body]. A person may not approve their own compensation or payroll changes.

## 10. Financial reporting and records

The [Treasurer/Finance Lead] will provide the governing body with reports at least [monthly/quarterly], including:

- Income and expenses compared with budget.
- Account balances and cash position.
- Restricted-fund balances.
- Outstanding obligations and material variances.
- A summary of unusual or significant transactions.

Financial records, receipts, approvals, bank statements, payroll records, and donor records must be retained for the periods required by law and the church’s records-retention schedule: [insert schedule]. Access must be limited to authorized people, and sensitive information must be stored securely.

## 11. Cash handling and exceptions

Cash received at events or services should be secured promptly, counted and documented by two people when practical, and deposited without using it for expenses. Any exception must be documented and approved by [role].

Exceptions to this policy require approval from [governing body/authorized officer], must be documented with the reason, and must not conflict with applicable law or donor restrictions.

## 12. Suspected errors, misuse, or fraud

Anyone who suspects an error, misuse of funds, fraud, or a control failure should promptly report it to [Treasurer/Board Chair/independent contact]. If the concern involves that person, report it to [alternate contact]. Reports will be handled discreetly and reviewed promptly. Retaliation against someone who raises a concern in good faith is prohibited.

## 13. Adoption and review

This policy takes effect when approved by [governing body] on [date]. It will be reviewed at least annually and updated when the church’s operations or applicable requirements change.
